2.

As per the writ petitioners, the Deputy Secretary (Revenue) published a notification in pursuance to the Right to Fair Compensation And Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 on 20.09.2016 acquiring the agricultural land for the purpose of construction of a dam.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation And Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In para 5.7 of the writ petition, it is mentioned that the petitioners were aware of the proceedings initiated by the authorities that without any field and actual survey, the Dindori Irrigation Project at 11 villages has been accorded technical and administrative approval in haste.
For this dam project which is being constructed on Seoni River, total 1256 hectares of land has been acquired, out of which 918 hectares of land is fertile private land.

3. On a specific question was put to the counsel for the petitioners regarding explanation with respect to considerable delay in filing the present writ petition as para 4 of the petition is silent with respect to the same, he submits that the petitioners are still in possession of the land in question.

But the fact remains that the acquisition proceedings were published on 20.09.2016 by issuance of a notification, which is put to challenge in the year 2023 by filing the present writ petition without there being any explanation for the delay and the land is sought to be acquired for the purpose of construction of a dam, which is in public interest.

The petitioners have approached this Court with considerable delay of almost seven years without there being any explanation for the same from the date of issuance of the notification and the fact that the acquisition of land is for construction of a dam i.e. in public interest.
Thus, no relief can be granted to the petitioner.
4. Thus, the writ petition sans merits and is accordingly dismissed.
No order as to costs.
(RAVI MALIMATH)
